topic: The glymphatic system and slow-wave sleep
body:
**During deep slow-wave sleep, your brain activates a clearance system called the glymphatic system. Cerebrospinal fluid is pumped through the brain's interstitial spaces, flushing out the metabolic waste that accumulated during the day.**

One of the primary targets of this process is amyloid-beta — a protein whose accumulation is associated with cognitive decline. Your brain produces it constantly while you're awake. Slow-wave sleep is when it gets cleared.

This system does not activate during light sleep. It does not activate during REM. It requires the specific neurological conditions of deep, slow-wave sleep — and it is disproportionately concentrated in the early cycles of the night, meaning early sleep timing matters more than most people realise.

You cannot replicate this process awake. There is no supplement, no device, no protocol that substitutes for it. The only way to run the clearance cycle is to give the brain the conditions it needs to reach slow-wave sleep consistently.

That's what sleep optimisation is actually about.

The full mechanism is in the guide — link in bio.
